weeks.d: An honest baseline, permission to tell the truth, and one weekend off-screen.
Give in a language that is not your own.
Wants, needs, demands — said out loud, finally.
Find every place the two of you go quiet.
One fear, under a microscope, with the cost of doing nothing.
Fix the mechanics before you touch the content.
The gridlocked thing has a dream buried in it.
Make the future specific enough to argue about.
Turn leaps into experiments you can actually run.
Make the calls. With dates. Out loud.
Execution, and the wobble that comes after deciding.
What changed, what stays, and the rhythm from here.

days.why: Before anything gets better you need a number you can come back to. Today is the number.
You are about to spend twelve weeks on the hard stuff. Start by remembering there is something worth doing it for.
Off the screen. Scissors, magazines, printouts, paper. Your hands will reach for things your explanations would have talked you out of.

days.t: Photograph it, then say what it means
days.why: A board on the wall becomes wallpaper inside a week. Photograph it, name what is actually on it, and pull the few that matter into the app so they cannot quietly disappear.
Most people give love in the currency they want to receive. It is the single most common reason two people who love each other both feel unloved.
Knowing your partner is a Words person is trivia. Spending in it daily is the practice.

days.t: What a good week looks like
days.why: You have both been assuming the other knows. Answer privately first — the gap between the two answers is the useful part.
You are going to hit weeks where one of you wants to quit. Write the rules now, while it is still easy.
Seven days of small data. Look at it before you go further.
You have a language you are bad at speaking. It is usually the one you did not grow up hearing.
Every couple has a museum of gifts that did not land. Those were not failures of love. They were currency errors.
Hinting is a tax you have both been paying. Today you stop.
Grand gestures are easier than daily ones, which is exactly why they do less.
Something you used to do fell off. Nobody decided to stop. It just stopped.
You have both been deflecting. It teaches the other person to stop trying.
Two weeks in. The easy part is nearly over.
Most fights are a need dressed as a demand, or a want being defended like a need. Sorting them lowers the stakes enormously.
You cannot negotiate a life together from vibes. You need the actual list.
Compatible people still have colliding values. Pretending otherwise is how the collision becomes a crash later.

days.t: The thing I have never told you I want
days.why: There is one. Both of you have one. Today is the day.
Every recurring complaint is a need wearing a bad costume.

days.t: The rhythm of what I need
days.why: Needs have frequencies. Most resentment is a weekly need being met annually.
You have named things this week that were unnamed for years. Do not skip past that.
Every couple has topics with a force field around them. You both feel it. Neither of you names it.
Avoidance is physical before it is verbal. If you can catch the body, you can catch the swerve.
Indecision is not neutral. It is a decision that keeps paying someone.
You have a shared vocabulary for postponing. Once you hear it, you cannot unhear it.

days.t: The cost of the last year
days.why: Not deciding has already cost you something. Today you price it.
A named decision behaves differently from a floating dread. Naming it does not commit you to anything.
The hardest four weeks are 4 through 7. You are one of them in.
You cannot examine four fears at once. Pick the one that is blocking the others.
Fear is vague on purpose. Vague fear cannot be argued with. Specific fear can.
Yesterday you named the disaster. Today you find out it has handles on it.
Everyone prices the risk of acting. Almost nobody prices the risk of staying exactly here.
Regret minimisation: project yourself far enough forward that the current fear stops being the loudest thing in the room.
Under most avoidance is something being guarded. It is rarely the thing you say it is.
One fear, fully examined. Notice whether it is still the same size.
Criticism, contempt, defensiveness and stonewalling predict how a couple ends better than what they fight about. Score yourself only.
Stonewalling is usually not indifference. It is a nervous system that has left the building. It has warning signs.
A break without a return time is abandonment. A break with one is a repair. Write the rule now, while you are calm.
A conversation ends roughly the way it starts. The first sixty seconds decide most of it.
It is not whether you fight. It is whether the brakes work mid-fight, and whether the other person lets them work.
Take a fight you actually had and replay it with the new machinery. Not to relitigate it — to practise.
The machinery week is done. Next week you point it at the thing that has never moved.
Perpetual problems are normal — most couples have several. Gridlock is different: the same argument, no movement, and it feels worse each time.
One of you speaks. One of you only asks questions. No solving, no defending, no negotiating. This structure is the entire point.
Same structure, roles reversed. Yesterday you were heard. Today you do the hearing.
Dreams are inherited. Understanding the inheritance does not settle the argument, but it stops it being an argument about who is unreasonable.
Inside every dream is a small non-negotiable core and a large negotiable outer layer. People fight over the outer layer thinking it is the core.
You are not solving this permanently today. You are designing something you can both live with for a set period, then review.
That was the hardest week. It gets more practical from here.
Dreams die in vagueness. Half the fear around a big move is fear of a number nobody has written down.
There is a difference between a risk that hurts and a risk you cannot come back from. Almost nothing is the second one.
You are not equally brave, and neither of you is wrong. The problem is when it is never discussed and just gets acted out.
Say the loss out loud. Unnamed, it is infinite. Named, it has edges.
Money can be recovered. The specific years you are in cannot.

days.t: What we are protecting that is not worth it
days.why: Some of what you are guarding stopped being valuable years ago. You are still paying the guard.
The constraint layer is mapped. Next week you get to build the thing you are constrained about.
Not goals. A scene. Write it in the present tense as though you are standing in it.
Ten years is far enough away that you stop being practical and start being honest.
Two futures, laid on top of each other. Where they line up is your shared project. Where they do not is your real work.
You each have three real non-negotiables. Everything else has been getting defended as though it were one.
Everything from nine weeks becomes objects you can move around. Vague futures cannot be prioritised. Cards can.
Do not rank by excitement or by feasibility. Rank by which one you would most regret never attempting.
You have a picture and a priority. Now it becomes an experiment rather than a leap.
Most of what people freeze on is reversible. Treating a two-way door like a one-way door is the most expensive mistake in this whole tool.
You do not have to decide the whole thing. You have to find the smallest version that produces real information.
An experiment without a written prediction is just a thing that happened.
If nothing could change your mind, you are not deciding. You are defending.
A plan without a calendar entry is a wish with better vocabulary.
Other people-s reactions are a real cost. Plan for them instead of being ambushed by them.
You have turned a frozen thing into a scheduled experiment. That is most of the work.
Couples stall because nobody agreed who decides. Write the constitution before you use it.
Today is not for exploring. Today you make a call and write it down.
The first one was hard. The second one is easier and that is the point — deciding is a muscle.
Some things genuinely should wait. Say which, why, and until when — so they stop leaking anxiety into everything else.

days.t: What we are saying no to
days.why: Every yes is several nos. Say them out loud so they are chosen instead of discovered later as resentment.
A decision you have not said outside the house is still reversible in a way that keeps you soft on it.
Look at the ledger. Eleven weeks ago none of this existed.
The gap between decided and started is where most of this dies. Close it today.
Three weeks after any real decision comes the wobble. It is predictable, it is not a signal, and it is much easier to survive if you wrote yourself a letter first.
Decisions that never touch a bank account tend not to be decisions.
You planned the announcement. Now plan the second conversation, which is the one that actually erodes people.
You are eight days from the end. Decide now what happens to this habit, or it will simply stop.

days.t: What we will be tempted to undo
days.why: Name the exit you are most likely to take, while you still think you would never take it.
One week left. Mostly consolidation from here.
The same four questions from day one. No looking at the old answers until you have both answered.
Write it privately so you get your own answer rather than the agreed one.
Be honest about the parts this did not fix. A tool that claims everything worked is not one you can trust next time.
Design something small enough that you will still be doing it in a year.
Ninety days from now is a real date. Something specific should be true by then.
Ninety days of small honest things. End it by saying the whole thing to each other in one place.
